content.text:
Here are some **notable art collaborations from 2023**, especially at the intersection of **fine art, fashion, museums, design, and public art**:

| Collaboration | Why it mattered |
|---|---|
| **Louis Vuitton x Yayoi Kusama** | One of the biggest art-fashion collaborations of 2023. Kusama’s signature dots, pumpkins, and infinity-net motifs appeared across Louis Vuitton bags, shoes, fragrances, store windows, and large-scale global installations. ([brandvelle.com](https://brandvelle.com/articles/louis-vuitton-yayoi-kusama-second-collaboration-2023?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Dior x Mickalene Thomas x Brooklyn Museum** | Artist **Mickalene Thomas** collaborated with Dior and the Brooklyn Museum on the 2023 Brooklyn Artists Ball, reimagining the museum’s Beaux-Arts Court with her visual language and scenographic approach. ([thecitylife.org](https://thecitylife.org/2023/03/01/brooklyn-museum-to-honor-carrie-mae-weems-at-2023-brooklyn-artists-ball-made-possible-by-dior/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **KAWS x Acute Art x Art Gallery of Ontario** | For **KAWS: FAMILY**, the AGO presented augmented-reality works created in collaboration with **Acute Art**, letting visitors interact with virtual KAWS sculptures via smartphone. ([ago.ca](https://ago.ca/press-release/art-and-pop-culture-collide-global-powerhouse-kaws-makes-canadian-museum-debut-ago?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MoMA x Adobe** | The Museum of Modern Art announced a multi-year partnership with Adobe in 2023 to support digital creativity, including a Creative Resident program where artists collaborate with MoMA. ([press.moma.org](https://press.moma.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/MoMA_Adobe_6.13.23.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Guggenheim Museum x Converse** | The Guggenheim and Converse announced a global partnership in 2023 aimed at supporting emerging artists, young creatives, and new forms of storytelling. ([guggenheim.org](https://www.guggenheim.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/press-release-converse-guggenheim-global-partnership-announcement-20231109.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **The Met x beauty/design brands** | The Metropolitan Museum of Art continued expanding art-based licensing collaborations with beauty, fragrance, jewelry, and nail-polish brands, using works from its collection as inspiration. ([harpersbazaar.com](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/beauty/makeup/a41780213/art-museums-beauty-collaborations/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **NOMA Creative Assembly 2023–24** | The New Orleans Museum of Art selected eight local artists for a residency-style program focused on collaborations with the museum’s collection, exhibitions, programs, and staff. ([noma.org](https://noma.org/creative-assembly-cohort-2023/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Beyond Granite: Pulling Together** | A 2023 public-art initiative on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., brought together multiple contemporary artists to rethink monuments, memory, and public space. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_Granite%3A_Pulling_Together?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Creativity Explored x Chronicle Books** | For Creativity Explored’s 40th anniversary, the organization partnered with Chronicle Books on *Art Is Art*, highlighting collaboration with neurodiverse artists. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity_Explored?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Axel Arigato x Alvin Armstrong** | A fashion-art collaboration where artist **Alvin Armstrong** translated the color palette and feeling of his 2023 painting *The Listening Skies* into apparel and accessories. ([wallpaper.com](https://www.wallpaper.com/art/fashion-meets-art-in-axel-arigato-and-alvin-armstrongs-colourful-collaboration?utm_source=openai)) |

If you mean **“art collaborations” for a school/project list**, the most recognizable 2023 example is probably **Louis Vuitton x Yayoi Kusama**, followed by **KAWS x Acute Art / AGO** and **MoMA x Adobe**.
